title: Orbital O4 follow-up MEASURED: the band PHASE SWEEP at fixed x over z in {31,50,71,100,200,400} x {2e5..1e10} (0.3 s, exact integers, the in-tree SieveOrbit definitions) - the 0181 phase table extended 5x in z. Findings: (1) THE LEVEL-1 BAND DOES NOT TIGHTEN: the relative width W/Phi grows in z - 6.56 (z=31) to 20.35 (z=400) at x = 1e10 (x3.1 over the sweep), for every x: deeper sieves WIDEN the band relative to the count; (2) the in-band position rho = (Phi - L1)/W drifts DOWN slowly in z (0.7166 to 0.6083 at x = 1e10), no sign of settling by z = 400, and is x-STABLE at fixed z (spread over x <= 2.2e-3 - the 0181 x-stability law persists at depth, degrading only mildly); (3) at z = 400 the first VISIBLE SPLIT between the main-term-based width and the count-based width appears: W/(xV) = 20.3414 vs W/Phi = 20.3517, i.e. Phi = 0.99950 xV - a 5.0e-4 deficit of the exact count from the sieve main term that the widths do not resolve until depth (the classical sieve error drifts in z; the band phase resolves it to relative 5e-4). The O4 'tightening vs position' question is answered at the measured level: ONLY the position evolves (and slowly), and it does not yet stabilize - the width grows. No RH claim: finite sieve combinatorics over exact integers; OFF-BOARD side-quest; MEASURED status only.
claim: Unit O4 of the orbital two-body side quest (docs/ORBITAL-TWO-BODY-SIDE-QUEST-2026-10-26.md): the cheap z-sweep follow-up of the 0181 phase table, measuring the phase diagram (x, z) -> (W/(xV), W/Phi, W/U2, rho, rho0) of the level-1 sieve band. Method: exact integers throughout - Phi by the memoized Legendre recursion (the in-tree phi_list semantics, SieveOrbit.lean 0180, triple-checked against the mu-sum and brute force in 0181), L1 = x - sum_p floor(x/p), W = sum_{p<q} floor(x/(pq)) (= U2 - L1 pairwise mass, theorem level1_width_eq_pairwise, 0184), V(z) = prod_{p<=z}(1 - 1/p) as an exact Fraction; the 0184 in-band invariant 0 <= Phi - L1 <= W asserted on all 36 rows as an identity check. Grid: z in {31, 50, 71, 100, 200, 400} (pi(z) in {11, 15, 20, 25, 46, 78}) at x in {2e5, 1e6, 1e7, 1e8, 1e9, 1e10}; wall time 0.3 s (the memoized recursion's state count is the smooth-quotient count, ~1e4 per x here). Measured facts: (1) W/(xV) (0181's number) and W/Phi agree to 4 decimals for z <= 200 (there Phi/xV = 1 within display precision) and SPLIT at z = 400: W/(xV) = 20.3414 vs W/Phi = 20.3517 at x = 1e10 -> Phi = 0.99950 * xV, a 5.0e-4 main-term deficit visible only at depth; (2) the relative width W/Phi grows monotonically in z at every x - at x = 1e10: 6.5598/8.3368/10.1249/11.6347/16.1088/20.3517 (ratio x3.1 from z = 31 to 400); the answer to the 0181-posed 'tightening vs position' question is: the band does NOT tighten - deeper sieves widen the level-1 band RELATIVE to the shrinking count (x3.1 in W/Phi over x12 in z); (3) rho = (Phi - L1)/W: 0.716630/0.692136/0.672878/0.659448/0.629134/0.608348 (x = 1e10, z = 31..400) - monotone slow decay, no settling; at fixed z the spread of rho over the six x-values: 1.35e-04 (z=31), 4.23e-04 (z=50), 3.00e-04 (z=71), 6.01e-04 (z=100), 1.89e-03 (z=200), 2.19e-03 (z=400) - the 0181 x-stability law survives at depth with a mild degradation (the small-x row x = 2e5 carries the wobble); (4) rho0 = Phi/U2 decays faster (0.34979 -> 0.11147 at x = 1e10): the count slides toward the lower edge of the WIDE band - both position readings (from L1 and from U2) move apart as the band grows, consistent with (1) and (2) jointly. Identity gate: 0184's in-band invariant holds on all 36 rows (asserted in the script; no violation at any (x, z) including the z = 400 rows where L1 is deeply negative, L1(1e10) ~ -1.3e10 at z = 400 - the band spans negative territory and rho remains a well-defined [0,1] position per 0184). What this is NOT: no law is asserted (the drift of rho and the growth law of W/Phi are recorded trajectories, not fits); the 5.0e-4 main-term deficit is a MEASURED instance of the classical sieve error at (x = 1e10, z = 400), not a bound; nothing here gates the mainstream (OFF-BOARD flank); no RH claim. Output: tmp/o4_out.txt (tables + the per-z x-stability spreads + the per-x z-trajectories). Next candidate when the main program names it: z beyond 400 (same recursion, state growth ~ smooth-quotient count) or the level-ladder extension (level k > 1 band phases - the conceptual question in the side-quest file section 4, named not scheduled).
